transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, well, I came in because I've been dealing with these really awful, unwanted thoughts. I'm an artist, and recently I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt. But while I was working on it, I just kept getting these thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like... if I made one wrong photo placement, or picked the wrong color, it would mean I didn’t love her enough. 

It wasn't just normal creative doubt. I couldn’t just brush them off, and it really unsettled me, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.

When these thoughts occur, do you feel compelled to perform any specific actions or mental rituals—like repeating phrases, rearranging items, or checking things—to try and prevent that sense of dishonor?

Yeah, I do. Um, I'll end up rereading the text for the labels, or just... nudging the same objects on my work table. And I'll check the layout photos over and over again. I just keep doing it until it finally feels "settled" in my head. Even though part of me knows it’s already perfectly fine and I’m really just losing studio time, I just feel like I have to do it until that feeling goes away.
When you have these thoughts, do you feel as though they are your own thoughts, or does it ever feel like they are being put into your mind by some outside force?

Um, no, they definitely feel like my own thoughts. It's just my own brain coming up with them. It doesn't feel like anyone or anything else is putting them there... it's just me worrying, I guess. Just really intense, stubborn worries that I can't seem to shut off.
On average, how much time each day do you spend having these thoughts and performing these repetitive actions?

Um, I'd say maybe... an hour or two a day, total? It's not taking up my entire day or anything, but it's definitely enough to be annoying and slow down my work. It usually happens in spurts while I'm in the studio.
Beyond the time it takes away from your studio work, do these thoughts and behaviors cause you significant distress or interfere with your relationships or other daily responsibilities?

Um, well, my relationships are mostly fine. And I am still getting most of my work done, generally. But... yeah, the extra time I end up losing in the studio has caused some real issues lately. Like, I actually missed a grant deadline recently because of it. And... I even backed out of a gallery talk that I had really wanted to do, just because I felt too behind to commit to it. So it is definitely getting in the way of my professional stuff, even if my day-to-day life is mostly okay.

Do you find yourself experiencing these types of intrusive thoughts or feeling the need to perform these repetitive actions in other areas of your life, such as at home or when you're out running errands?

No, not really. It seems to be pretty isolated to my studio space. Um, when I'm at home relaxing or just out grocery shopping or whatever, I don't really have those same worries, and I don't feel the need to do any of those routines. It really just happens when I'm working on my art.

When you are in your studio, do you find that your need to repeat these actions is driven specifically by a need for things to be perfectly symmetrical, aligned, or 'just right' in their physical placement?

Um, no, I wouldn't say so. It's not really about making things symmetrical or perfectly lined up. To be honest, my studio is actually kind of cluttered, so I don't really have that feeling that my tools or materials need to be placed 'just right' or anything like that. It's really not about the physical placement of things for me.

When you are repeating these actions in the studio, are you performing them specifically to prevent the 'dishonor' you fear, or do you feel a sense of internal pressure to perform them in a very specific, rigid sequence?

Um, it's not really a rigid sequence, exactly. It's more about doing it until I get this specific feeling. Like, I’ll end up rereading the label text for a piece, or... nudging the same objects on the work table, and just checking my layout photos over and over again. I basically just keep doing all that until it finally feels, I don't know, 'settled' in my head. It's frustrating because part of me completely knows it’s already fine, and I’m just losing studio time, but I still feel like I have to do it until that settled feeling happens.

When you feel that internal pressure to repeat those actions, are you doing it because you are afraid that something terrible will happen if you don't, or is it more just to relieve the discomfort of that 'unsettled' feeling?

It's definitely just to relieve the discomfort. I'm not really afraid that something terrible is going to happen or anything like that. Like I was just saying with the rereading and nudging the objects on my table... it really is just to get rid of that unsettled feeling. I'll keep checking those layout photos over and over purely to make that feeling go away. I know the piece is already fine, and I'm just losing my studio time doing it, but I just can't seem to move on to the next step until that specific discomfort stops.
When you feel that 'unsettled' feeling in your studio, would you describe it more as a sense of incompleteness, or is it more like a feeling of mental tension or anxiety that you need to resolve?

I'm not totally sure how to label it, to be honest. It's just... a really uncomfortable feeling that something isn't quite done or right yet. I wouldn't necessarily call it anxiety, like my heart isn't racing or anything. It's just this mental itch, I guess, that I can't ignore until I do the things and it finally feels settled.

When you have that 'itch' that something isn't quite done, does it feel like you are trying to prevent a specific, catastrophic outcome, or is the drive simply to achieve a sense of 'completeness' or 'just rightness'?

Um, yeah, it's definitely just about getting that sense of completeness. Like I mentioned before, I'm not worried about any kind of catastrophe or disaster happening if I don't do it. It really is just... trying to get things to feel right. Once it finally hits that point where it feels just right, the itch goes away and I can actually get back to work.
